author: Restructuring__ (@Restructuring__)
text:
Really great data from BBG / Moody, some thoughts:
- People might think that protections like J. Crew are always included, but the data tells a very different story
- Of 158 high-yield bonds surveyed in 2025, only 32% contained so-called J. Crew blockers, up from 20% in 2024
- Protections for very famous LMEs like Pluralsight and Envision are still very rare at 5% of the market; perfect example of the negotiating power of issuers in times of strong capital markets
- There is a very linear correlation between time from the first LME and % of protection included (J. Crew is the oldest and now it is the most protected, etc.); that said, the time needed for these protections to regularly flow in is really long (decades)

I plan to have a dedicated writeup on the current LME landscape from the creditor perspective, but this graph makes the perfect case: leveraged finance market has, for better or worse, settled into an equilibrium in which newly issued credit agreements are loose by default

author: StockMarket.News (@_Investinq)
text:
Disney handed the keys to Mickey Mouse, Darth Vader, and the entire Marvel universe to an AI company, and three months later that company killed the product.

Nobody in Hollywood saw the ending coming this fast.

In December 2025, Disney CEO Bob Iger signed a $1 billion investment deal with OpenAI built around a video generator called Sora.

The terms were staggering, over 200 characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Star Wars were licensed to an AI platform that would let fans generate short videos featuring their favorite heroes.

Disney would stream that content directly on Disney+, and Iger publicly called it the future of storytelling.

The deal had one fatal flaw hiding inside the fine print.

It was built entirely on a product that OpenAI was losing confidence in, as Sora downloads cratered after launch and the app never found a mainstream audience.

The technology was real but the demand was not.

And today, OpenAI pulled the plug completely.

The company officially shut down Sora as a standalone app, sunsetting Sora 1 for US users on March 13 and announcing a full platform shutdown shortly after.

The Disney investment had nothing left to stand on, and a Disney spokesperson confirmed it.

Nobody knows exactly how much money already changed hands between the two companies, and nobody knows yet whether Disney recovers any of it.

The most valuable IP library on the planet had been cracked open and the company it was handed to simply walked away.

OpenAI, meanwhile, is chasing a completely different vision, a desktop superapp that merges ChatGPT, its browser, and its coding tools into a single platform aimed at enterprise customers.

The company told employees internally it had been "dispersing efforts across too many apps," and Sora was the casualty of that reckoning.

author: Tanay Jaipuria (@tanayj)
text:
Cursor's Composer 2 technical report is fantastic. Some of my notes:

- Base model is Kimi K2.5. Also Considered GLM‑5, Deepseek v3.2
- Two-stage training: continued pretraining on code-heavy data, then large-scale RL
- Tasks used for RL were based on representative Cursor usage (iterating on features, debugging most represented)
- Training stack built on Ray + PyTorch. Fully asynchronous with independent training and rollout generation workers
- RL Training environments run on Firecracker VMs via an internal platform called Anyrun
- RL inference runs on Fireworks AI
- Developed own evals (Cursorbench-3) where tasks require ~10x more lines changed and have shorter instructions than SWE-bench
- Composer2 is close to SOTA on their evals and much cheaper than other models with similar performance

output.summary: Cursor Composer 2技术报告：采用Kimi K2.5基模，双阶段训练+大规模RL，eval接近SOTA且成本更低

author: 区块链行情研究 (@qkl2058)
text:
昨天凌晨三点，Claude Code给我打了个电话。

我迷迷糊糊拿起手机，屏幕上弹出一条消息：“钱包在11美分时买入BTC看涨。要打开Polymarket吗？”

我说了声“是”，就继续睡了。

然后Claude Code自己解锁了我的备用手机，打开Polymarket，找到对应的市场，填好金额，点了买入。我在笔记本的网页界面上看得一清二楚，手机截图每秒都在刷新。到早上的时候，那个仓位已经盈利平掉了。

跟你说说我是怎么弄到这个程度的。

一周前，我让Claude Code写个脚本，从Polymarket拉链上数据，按照15分钟BTC市场的胜率给钱包排个名。二十分钟后，我拿到了一张表格，里面有几百个地址，其中有一个明显不一样——每天两百多笔交易，入场时机非常准，盈利曲线一路往上走。

我把这个地址扔回给Claude Code，让它分析一下策略。结果发现，这个钱包每100毫秒就在监控Binance和Bybit上的BTC波动率，等波动率降到0.08%以下的时候，同时用25到35美分的价格买入看涨和看跌。

这是个标准的跨式策略：一边亏掉，另一边能飞到1美元，每笔仓位能赚个三到四倍。一天能跑几十次。

我想跟单，但这玩意儿信号随时会来，总不能每十五分钟爬起来看一眼。所以我又搭了个东西。

拿了部旧安卓手机，装了一个基于Qwen3-VL视觉模型的代理。这个代理能看懂屏幕上发生了什么，然后通过ADB模拟人操作——点一下、滑动、输入文字。再把它接到Claude Code上当执行器。

现在的流程是这样的：Claude Code盯着那个钱包，发现新仓位就给我打电话。我说“行”，或者三十秒没接，手机上那个代理就会自己打开Polymarket，把单子给跟进去。

说白了，我用两个AI搭了个自动驾驶系统——一个负责想，一个负责按按钮。我该睡觉睡觉，偶尔接个电话就行。

→ 这是整个系统追踪的钱包：https://t.co/XXfblWBlJL

如果不想自己折腾这套系统，有个Telegram机器人能把第一步给做了：跟踪这个钱包，每次新入场的时候发个信号过来：https://t.co/EgT16k3fC5

AI凌晨三点打电话问我能不能花我的钱。

一年前这事儿听着像精神分裂，现在也就是个普通的星期一。
